How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.

### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`

The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.

`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`

```yaml
# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
validate:
  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
  next: load
load:
  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
  next: apply
apply:
  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save
save:
  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
```

```java
// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
public class ValidateOwner {
  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
  }
}
public class LoadOwner {
  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
    ownerOut.set(owner);
  }
}
public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
  }
}
public class SaveOwner {
  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
    repository.save(owner);
  }
}
public class RespondWithOwner {
  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
  }
}
```

`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`

```yaml
handle:
  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
```

```java
public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
  }
}
```

### Step wiring

Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
`method:`.

- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
  as `@Parameter T`.
- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
  branch; not calling it short-circuits.

### Function parameters

Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:

- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.

### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`

Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):

- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.

### Naming

Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).

Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
responder. Steps in between work with entities.

### Request body and validation

- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
  first step publishes it as a variable.
- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
  invalid body can return 400.

### Transactions

`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.

### Errors

Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.

### Security

Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:

```yaml
composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
```

/** After the change's own audit lines: a ROLLUP line per person whose figures moved, then TOTALS
 *  when a sheet total moved; nothing when no figure moved. */
public class RecordRollup {
    public void record(@PathVariable("sheetId") String sheetId,
            @RequestParam(name = "by", required = false) String by, @Val Rollup before,
            PersonRepository people, ClaimRepository claims, RateRepository rates,
            SheetRepository sheets, SettingRepository settings, Audit audit) {
        String id = sheetId.trim();
        Rollup after = Rollup.of(id, people, claims, rates, sheets, settings);
        for (String line : after.changesSince(before, id, by == null ? "" : by)) {
            audit.record(line);
        }
    }
}
package net.officefloor.hq.app.rollup;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.Claim;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.ClaimRepository;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.ClaimStatus;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.Dues;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.person.Person;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.person.PersonRepository;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.rate.Rate;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.rate.RateRepository;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.setting.DatedSetting;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.setting.SettingRepository;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.sheet.SheetRepository;

/** The sheet's figures at one moment, as the screen shows them: each person's claimed (corrections
 *  left out) and
 *  due-total (null: n/a; else at most the sheet's cap) and overdue-total, in the order they were added, and the
 *  sheet's claimed-total, due-total and overdue-total (these two leave out the single highest and
 *  lowest person's figure when three or more people have one), with the sheet's alert threshold
 *  (null: off). */
public record Rollup(Map<Long, Figures> people, String claimedTotal, String dueTotal, String overdueTotal,
        BigDecimal alertThreshold) {

    /** A person's figures: their name, claimed, due-total (null: n/a) and overdue-total (the shown
     *  dues of their open claims past their due-by plus grace days on the sheet's today, n/a ones skipped). */
    public record Figures(String name, String claimed, String dueTotal, String overdueTotal) {
        public boolean sameAs(Figures other) {
            return other != null && claimed.equals(other.claimed)
                    && (dueTotal == null ? other.dueTotal == null : dueTotal.equals(other.dueTotal))
                    && overdueTotal.equals(other.overdueTotal);
        }
    }

    /** The sheet's figures now. */
    public static Rollup of(String sheetId, PersonRepository people, ClaimRepository claims,
            RateRepository rates, SheetRepository sheets, SettingRepository settings) {
        List<Rate> sheetRates = rates.list(sheetId);
        DatedSetting floor = settings.floor(sheetId);
        BigDecimal cap = settings.cap(sheetId);
        LocalDate todayDate = sheets.today(sheetId);
        String today = todayDate.toString();
        Dues.Late late = settings.late(sheetId, todayDate);
        List<Claim> all = claims.list(sheetId);
        Map<Long, Figures> figures = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        BigDecimal claimedTotal = zero();
        List<BigDecimal> dues = new ArrayList<>();
        List<BigDecimal> overdues = new ArrayList<>();
        for (Person p : people.list(sheetId)) {
            BigDecimal claimed = zero();
            BigDecimal due = zero();
            BigDecimal overdue = zero();
            boolean kept = false;
            for (Claim c : all) {
                if (c.getPersonId() != p.getId() || !p.countsLive(c)) continue;
                if (!corrects(c)) claimed = claimed.add(new BigDecimal(c.getAmount()));
                String grade = p.gradeOn(c.getDate());
                String pct = rateOn(sheetRates, grade, c.getDate());
                String d = Dues.shown(c, pct == null ? null : Dues.of(c.getAmount(), pct, late.rounding(c.getRoundDate())), floor.on(c.getDate()), late);
                kept |= c.getSettledDue() != null || c.isBound()
                        || (pct != null && (!grade.equals(p.getGrade()) || c.getDate().compareTo(today) <= 0));
                if (d != null) due = due.add(new BigDecimal(d));
                if (d != null && ClaimStatus.isOpen(c.getStatus()) && late.lateFrom(c).isBefore(todayDate)) {
                    overdue = overdue.add(new BigDecimal(d));
                }
            }
            boolean na = rateOn(sheetRates, p.getGrade(), today) == null && !kept;
            if (cap != null && due.compareTo(cap) > 0) due = cap.setScale(2);
            figures.put(p.getId(), new Figures(p.getName(), claimed.toPlainString(),
                    na ? null : due.toPlainString(), overdue.toPlainString()));
            claimedTotal = claimedTotal.add(claimed);
            if (!na) dues.add(due);
            overdues.add(overdue);
        }
        return new Rollup(figures, claimedTotal.toPlainString(), trimmedSum(dues).toPlainString(),
                trimmedSum(overdues).toPlainString(), settings.alertThreshold(sheetId));
    }

    /** The audit lines after a change from {@code before} to this: one ROLLUP per person whose
     *  figures moved (a new person counts as moved), then TOTALS when a sheet total moved, then an
     *  ALERT per person (in list order) whose due-total went from at or below the alert threshold
     *  (or none) to above it. */
    public List<String> changesSince(Rollup before, String sheetId, String by) {
        String head = " sheet=" + sheetId + " by=" + by;
        List<String> lines = new ArrayList<>();
        people.forEach((id, now) -> {
            if (!now.sameAs(before.people.get(id))) {
                lines.add("ROLLUP" + head + " person=" + now.name() + " claimed=" + now.claimed()
                        + " due-total=" + (now.dueTotal() == null ? "n/a" : now.dueTotal())
                        + " overdue-total=" + now.overdueTotal());
            }
        });
        if (!claimedTotal.equals(before.claimedTotal) || !dueTotal.equals(before.dueTotal)
                || !overdueTotal.equals(before.overdueTotal)) {
            lines.add("TOTALS" + head + " claimed-total=" + claimedTotal + " due-total=" + dueTotal
                    + " overdue-total=" + overdueTotal);
        }
        if (alertThreshold != null) {
            people.forEach((id, now) -> {
                Figures was = before.people.get(id);
                if (above(now) && (was == null || !above(was))) {
                    lines.add("ALERT" + head + " name=" + now.name() + " due-total=" + now.dueTotal());
                }
            });
        }
        return lines;
    }

    /** Whether the person's due-total is above the alert threshold (none: not). */
    private boolean above(Figures figures) {
        return figures.dueTotal() != null && new BigDecimal(figures.dueTotal()).compareTo(alertThreshold) > 0;
    }

    /** Whether the claim corrects another: such a claim is left out of claimed. */
    private static boolean corrects(Claim c) {
        return c.getCorrects() != null && !c.getCorrects().isBlank();
    }

    /** The grade's rate in force on the date (yyyy-MM-dd), inherited up the parent chain; null when none. */
    private static String rateOn(List<Rate> rates, String grade, String date) {
        Rate found = RateRepository.inForce(rates, grade, date);
        return found == null ? null : found.pct();
    }

    /** The figures added up, leaving out the single highest and the single lowest when there are three or more. */
    private static BigDecimal trimmedSum(List<BigDecimal> figures) {
        List<BigDecimal> sorted = new ArrayList<>(figures);
        sorted.sort(BigDecimal::compareTo);
        if (sorted.size() >= 3) sorted = sorted.subList(1, sorted.size() - 1);
        BigDecimal total = zero();
        for (BigDecimal f : sorted) total = total.add(f);
        return total;
    }

    private static BigDecimal zero() {
        return BigDecimal.ZERO.setScale(2);
    }
}

/** After the change's own audit lines: a ROLLUP line per person whose figures moved, then TOTALS
 *  when a sheet total moved; nothing when no figure moved. */
public class RecordRollup {
    public void record(@PathVariable("sheetId") String sheetId,
            @RequestParam(name = "by", required = false) String by, @Val Rollup before,
            PersonRepository people, ClaimRepository claims, RateRepository rates,
            SheetRepository sheets, SettingRepository settings, Audit audit) {
        String id = sheetId.trim();
        Rollup after = Rollup.of(id, people, claims, rates, sheets, settings);
        for (String line : after.changesSince(before, id, by == null ? "" : by)) {
            audit.record(line);
        }
    }
}
package net.officefloor.hq.app.rollup;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.Claim;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.ClaimRepository;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.ClaimStatus;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.Dues;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.person.Person;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.person.PersonRepository;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.rate.Rate;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.rate.RateRepository;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.setting.DatedSetting;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.setting.SettingRepository;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.sheet.SheetRepository;

/** The sheet's figures at one moment, as the screen shows them: each person's claimed (corrections
 *  left out) and
 *  due-total (null: n/a; else at most the sheet's cap) and overdue-total, in the order they were added, and the
 *  sheet's claimed-total, due-total and overdue-total (these two leave out the single highest and
 *  lowest person's figure when three or more people have one), with the sheet's alert threshold
 *  (null: off). */
public record Rollup(Map<Long, Figures> people, String claimedTotal, String dueTotal, String overdueTotal,
        BigDecimal alertThreshold) {

    /** A person's figures: their name, claimed, due-total (null: n/a) and overdue-total (the shown
     *  dues of their open claims past their due-by plus grace days on the sheet's today, n/a ones skipped). */
    public record Figures(String name, String claimed, String dueTotal, String overdueTotal) {
        public boolean sameAs(Figures other) {
            return other != null && claimed.equals(other.claimed)
                    && (dueTotal == null ? other.dueTotal == null : dueTotal.equals(other.dueTotal))
                    && overdueTotal.equals(other.overdueTotal);
        }
    }

    /** The sheet's figures now. */
    public static Rollup of(String sheetId, PersonRepository people, ClaimRepository claims,
            RateRepository rates, SheetRepository sheets, SettingRepository settings) {
        List<Rate> sheetRates = rates.list(sheetId);
        DatedSetting floor = settings.floor(sheetId);
        BigDecimal cap = settings.cap(sheetId);
        LocalDate todayDate = sheets.today(sheetId);
        String today = todayDate.toString();
        Dues.Late late = settings.late(sheetId, todayDate);
        List<Claim> all = claims.list(sheetId);
        Map<Long, Figures> figures = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        BigDecimal claimedTotal = zero();
        List<BigDecimal> dues = new ArrayList<>();
        List<BigDecimal> overdues = new ArrayList<>();
        for (Person p : people.list(sheetId)) {
            BigDecimal claimed = zero();
            BigDecimal due = zero();
            BigDecimal overdue = zero();
            boolean kept = false;
            for (Claim c : all) {
                if (c.getPersonId() != p.getId() || !p.countsLive(c)) continue;
                if (!corrects(c)) claimed = claimed.add(new BigDecimal(c.getAmount()));
                String grade = p.gradeOn(c.getDate());
                String pct = rateOn(sheetRates, grade, c.getDate());
                String d = Dues.shown(c, pct == null ? null : Dues.of(c.getAmount(), pct, late.rounding(c.getRoundDate())), floor.on(c.getDate()), late);
                kept |= c.getSettledDue() != null || c.isBound()
                        || (pct != null && (!grade.equals(p.getGrade()) || c.getDate().compareTo(today) <= 0));
                if (d != null) due = due.add(new BigDecimal(d));
                if (d != null && ClaimStatus.isOpen(c.getStatus()) && late.lateFrom(c).isBefore(todayDate)) {
                    overdue = overdue.add(new BigDecimal(d));
                }
            }
            boolean na = rateOn(sheetRates, p.getGrade(), today) == null && !kept;
            if (cap != null && due.compareTo(cap) > 0) due = cap.setScale(2);
            figures.put(p.getId(), new Figures(p.getName(), claimed.toPlainString(),
                    na ? null : due.toPlainString(), overdue.toPlainString()));
            claimedTotal = claimedTotal.add(claimed);
            if (!na) dues.add(due);
            overdues.add(overdue);
        }
        return new Rollup(figures, claimedTotal.toPlainString(), trimmedSum(dues).toPlainString(),
                trimmedSum(overdues).toPlainString(), settings.alertThreshold(sheetId));
    }

    /** The audit lines after a change from {@code before} to this: one ROLLUP per person whose
     *  figures moved (a new person counts as moved), then TOTALS when a sheet total moved, then an
     *  ALERT per person (in list order) whose due-total went from at or below the alert threshold
     *  (or none) to above it. */
    public List<String> changesSince(Rollup before, String sheetId, String by) {
        String head = " sheet=" + sheetId + " by=" + by;
        List<String> lines = new ArrayList<>();
        people.forEach((id, now) -> {
            if (!now.sameAs(before.people.get(id))) {
                lines.add("ROLLUP" + head + " person=" + now.name() + " claimed=" + now.claimed()
                        + " due-total=" + (now.dueTotal() == null ? "n/a" : now.dueTotal())
                        + " overdue-total=" + now.overdueTotal());
            }
        });
        if (!claimedTotal.equals(before.claimedTotal) || !dueTotal.equals(before.dueTotal)
                || !overdueTotal.equals(before.overdueTotal)) {
            lines.add("TOTALS" + head + " claimed-total=" + claimedTotal + " due-total=" + dueTotal
                    + " overdue-total=" + overdueTotal);
        }
        if (alertThreshold != null) {
            people.forEach((id, now) -> {
                Figures was = before.people.get(id);
                if (above(now) && (was == null || !above(was))) {
                    lines.add("ALERT" + head + " name=" + now.name() + " due-total=" + now.dueTotal());
                }
            });
        }
        return lines;
    }

    /** Whether the person's due-total is above the alert threshold (none: not). */
    private boolean above(Figures figures) {
        return figures.dueTotal() != null && new BigDecimal(figures.dueTotal()).compareTo(alertThreshold) > 0;
    }

    /** Whether the claim corrects another: such a claim is left out of claimed. */
    private static boolean corrects(Claim c) {
        return c.getCorrects() != null && !c.getCorrects().isBlank();
    }

    /** The grade's rate in force on the date (yyyy-MM-dd), inherited up the parent chain; null when none. */
    private static String rateOn(List<Rate> rates, String grade, String date) {
        Rate found = RateRepository.inForce(rates, grade, date);
        return found == null ? null : found.pct();
    }

    /** The figures added up, leaving out the single highest and the single lowest when there are three or more. */
    private static BigDecimal trimmedSum(List<BigDecimal> figures) {
        List<BigDecimal> sorted = new ArrayList<>(figures);
        sorted.sort(BigDecimal::compareTo);
        if (sorted.size() >= 3) sorted = sorted.subList(1, sorted.size() - 1);
        BigDecimal total = zero();
        for (BigDecimal f : sorted) total = total.add(f);
        return total;
    }

    private static BigDecimal zero() {
        return BigDecimal.ZERO.setScale(2);
    }
}

Retired members, members with a hold in force today, and members outside their from/to dates get 0 or blank. The remainder goes to the smallest non-zero cut. Per period, the due and the change from the previous period. Counts per status and per void reason. - **ALERT**: written to the audit file when a person's due-total crosses above `alert-threshold`. ## Who may do what - **Roles** (`RoleRepository.roleOf`): clerk is the default. A user is a steward while a delegation covers today; only a steward by assignment may delegate. A viewer may change nothing, and an archived sheet refuses every change (`RefuseViewer`). The as-of view (`AsOfFilter`) refuses every change. - **Permission matrix** (`Permissions`, `perm-`): open, settle, void and close default to clerk and steward; reassign and reopen default to steward. - **Steward only**: approve, reject (needs a reason), re-settle, re-date, cancel a statement, merge, transfer, archive, and voiding a SETTLED claim (within `SETTLED_DAYS` = 7 days of its settlement; this reverses its figure). - **Four eyes**: the user who opened a claim, or last edited it, may not settle or approve it. - **Clerk limit**: when a clerk settles a claim whose due is above `clerk-limit`, it goes to PENDING with nothing frozen. - **Proof threshold** (`requireProof`): a claim whose due is above `proof-threshold-`, else `proof-threshold`, needs at least one proof before it can be settled or approved. - **Note threshold** (`requireNote`): a claim whose due is above it cannot be opened with an empty note. - **Period cap** (`requireUnderCap`): limits how many open claims a person may have per period. ## What freezes, and when - **Settle / approve** freezes `settledDue`: the shown due, including that day's late charge and floor. **Re-settle** freezes it again as if the claim were open and unbound. - **Close or soft-close** freezes `closedTotal` and `personTotals` (`PeriodClosing.fixNow`). A hard close then refuses add, edit, lock, open, settle, approve, reject, void, defer, reassign, re-date, split, add proof, add line and delete for any claim whose due-by is in the period (`requireOpen`). Soft close freezes the figures only. Reopen unfreezes. **Auto-close**: when today changes and `grace-days` is set, open periods with to-date + grace-days before the new today are closed. - **Restore** works only on the same sheet's today the claim was deleted. A new today releases all claim locks. ## What dates decide - The **claim's date** picks the grade, rate, floor, terms, grace days, proof and note thresholds (each in force on that date), the rounding (via `roundDate`), the age buckets, active, backing, and holds and retirements. - The **due-by** picks the period, the number and overdue status. - **Today** picks the cap, the clerk limit, the late charge and the current grade. - A **blank date** means `entry-date`, else today, when adding (`AddClaim`, paste, quick-add). When editing (`ApplyClaim`) it means today. - **Retirement**: a claim dated after `retiredFrom`, or inside a past retirement, is refused. ## Import, paste, plans and hold - **ImportPeople**: all or nothing. A line matching a name or alias edits that person (grade from today; terms and contact only if given); otherwise it adds a person. Tree-name clashes and duplicate contacts are refused. - **PasteClaims**: all or nothing; adds DRAFTs, checked as `AddClaim` checks a claim. - **GeneratePlanClaims**: makes DRAFTs up to today, skipping dates that are refused. - **Bulk settle** is all or nothing and stamps a batch number; **bulk open** works claim by claim. - **Hold**: changes no stored data. It only removes unbound open claims from the live totals and from pool cuts. # 2. How easy this was to follow It is hard to follow. There is no single place that holds the rules. Each figure is computed twice, in Java (`Dues`, `Rollup`, `PeriodClosing`, `TakeStatement`, plus the "rate → `Dues.of` → `Dues.shown`" sequence pasted into five or more step classes) and again in TypeScript (`rates/api.ts`, `claims/api.ts`, `periods/api.ts`, `settings/api.ts`). Some rules exist only in the front end (backing, active, aged, tag totals), and the permission checks are spread across roughly a hundred one-method step classes. The comments are detailed but sometimes wrong: - `ClosePeriod`'s comment says a claim belongs to a period by its date; the code uses its due-by. - The front end describes claim numbers as "sheet-wide 1, 2, …"; the server gives `FY-`. - The holiday and due-by comments in `settings/api.ts` and `claims/api.ts` describe a calendar-day rule; the server counts business days. - Holds are described as affecting OPEN claims; the code applies them to OPEN and PENDING claims. So a new developer has to cross-check both copies and the code itself rather than trust any one description.
